decisions.assessment: Two CC0 preserved specimens are returned for the exact waterBody text Bay River. Both share the 1941-10-16 event date and a coordinate with 1,743 m uncertainty; their locality is only ?3 km from Laguna de Bay.? This is geographically plausible for the Atlas-listed Bay River locality but does not establish that either specimen came from that river channel.
decisions.decision: Keep as historical candidate records only. Add no species assertion until primary collection/locality documentation resolves site identity and suitability of coordinates.

decisions.assessment: The same preserved specimen is returned by both text fields. The record states stateProvince Rizal, coordinates 15.706832, 121.111876 and 13,748 m coordinate uncertainty, while this Atlas lead is currently associated with Laguna. The coordinates/state do not support the Laguna river identity.
decisions.decision: Do not attribute to this lead. No species assertion; resolve through the CAS catalogue/record provenance and visual verification of the Atlas table.

decision.interpretation: A zero means no matching Actinopterygii record was returned by these exact-string field searches under the selected checklist and country filter. It does not show that fish are absent. Nonzero text matches are candidates, not waterbody-specific biological evidence, until the collection locality and feature identity are adjudicated.

limitations: The 40 searches used only exact Atlas name strings in waterBody/locality, PH, and the selected Actinopterygii taxonomy; alternate spellings, synonyms and other fields were not searched.
The Bay River candidate records provide broad locality context only; no exact river reach has been verified.
The San Cristobal text hit has conflicting province/coordinates and large uncertainty; it is not used as evidence for the Laguna lead.
GBIF occurrence availability does not establish current presence, abundance, catchability, diet, salinity, safety or legal status.
The Atlas crosswalk itself is a selected historical inventory, not a complete river denominator; its asterisk meaning and public-derived-data reuse fit remain unresolved.
